source: Saved per-image attack results; no new attacks.
limitations: This is a comparison of recorded deployments, not an isolated causal effect of runtime.
Four source families differ in architecture/training; graphs, calibration and quantizers also differ.
Conditioning on every deployment and FP32 reference being clean-correct changes the pilot population.
BPDA derivatives differ between runtimes; smaller attack success does not establish genuine robustness.
QNN ResNetV2 (superseded) used TorchVision INT8 gradients on a timm target; its gradient results are excluded from ranking and retained only as a record of that error.
QNN uses no native autograd: BPDA scores every forward on the device and takes derivatives from the reconstructed FP32 source.
QNN has no independently saved image-hash manifest for the V1 run; alignment uses saved configuration, labels and recovered control predictions.
The matched QNN source is reconstructed from the documented QAIRT ONNX; no hash-linked chain to the compiled binary is established, though the board context hash is recorded and verified each run.
All measurements concern one 100-image, ten-class seed, digital cropped continuous-pixel attacks and finite query budgets.

qnn_control_alignment.limitation: This corroborates the retained control alignment; it does not replace a missing attack-time board image-hash manifest.
